scope: Semantic holder audit and Wan repair retries for the ten-second EPIC Ego bottle handover
summary: The previously published Wan handover and two semantics-heavy prompt retries all failed the terminal-holder contract: the blue bottle stayed in or moved toward the screen-right gripper. They are rejected from delivery even though the older visual-only gate had accepted the first candidate.
evidence: The old seed-42 output has 0.970833 valid blue-bottle tracking, final-two-second median normalized x 0.597814, final p90 x 0.627677, and first-to-final leftward shift -0.106851; it fails the screen-left terminal-holder and net-transfer checks.
Seed 43 has final median x 0.613788, p90 x 0.634169, and leftward shift -0.119233; seed 44 has final median x 0.625621, p90 x 0.650158, and leftward shift -0.128471.
Dense review confirms that none of the three Wan candidates ends with the bottle enclosed only by the screen-left gripper and the screen-right gripper empty and separated.
The evaluator now adds an automatic saturated-blue bottle trajectory gate and an independent dense contact/release review gate.
lessons: A generic task-adherence review is insufficient for a handover; the terminal object holder and release ordering must be measured explicitly.
Prompt emphasis cannot rescue a model route that consistently violates the holder transition, so candidate routing should switch models instead of weakening the gate.
limitations: The blue-bottle gate measures camera-frame position and cannot establish force closure or physical contact.
The rejected retry set covers seeds 42-44 for this route and prompt family, not every possible Wan configuration.
next_actions: Promote a different generated route only after both the automatic screen-left transfer gate and dense left-close/right-open review pass.
